title: Plural genitive of common diphthong words
summary: Drop the first vowel of ie, yö or uo before -iden or -itten in these one-syllable words: tie (“road”) → teiden.
targetSkills: Plural genitive of common diphthong words
objectives: Drop the first vowel of ie, yö or uo before -iden or -itten in these one-syllable words: tie (“road”) → teiden.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A plural genitive refers to more than one person or thing. Its ending belongs to the plural modifier, not necessarily to the thing owned. Here the task is forming the word.
Drop the first vowel of ie, yö or uo before -iden or -itten in these one-syllable words. Both alternatives are standard.
keyPoints: Learn the word with its stem; the last letter alone does not identify every pattern.

steps: Drop i from ie: tie → te-; add -iden or -itten.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.
